_comment: Mutation testing answers what coverage cannot: would these tests actually catch a bug? Stryker introduces defects on purpose and reports how many the suite fails to notice. Run with `npm run test:mutation`; it is slow by design and not part of `npm run check`. The json reporter is on so a run leaves machine-readable output: without it reports/ kept a mutation.json from an older run, which reads exactly like a fresh one and reports different line numbers.
_comment_the_score_can_fall_as_the_suite: A timeout counts as a kill, so the headline rewards a slow machine. Measured across three runs while the suite only ever gained tests: 82.07 with 77 timeouts, 81.09 with 22, 80.88 with 8. Kills rose 1846 -> 1887 the whole way; the score fell, because timeouts had been masking survivors. 0.3.0 shipped at 80.96 with 1889 kills. Compare killed and survived counts, never two headline numbers. A loaded CI runner scores HIGHER, so `break` is set against the least-timeout run — the honest floor.
_comment_verify_by_hand: A survivor is a lead, not a verdict. With coverageAnalysis perTest, Stryker has reported mutants as survived that the suite does in fact kill — confirmed by applying the mutation by hand and watching it go red. Do that before writing a test for one.
